title: Steel Strips Wheels Ltd-$ - 513262 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Steel Strips Wheels Q4 FY26 revenue up about 20% YoY to INR 1,475 crore; management guides FY27 EBITDA per wheel near INR 300 and EBITDA INR 650 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 1,475 crore (about 20% YoY) with EBITDA including other income of INR 152.52 crore, the company's highest ever quarter, and Q4 EBITDA per wheel of INR 282. Full-year FY26 revenue rose 17% to INR 5,183 crore and EBITDA including other income reached INR 523 crore, but PAT fell slightly to INR 202 crore on about INR 28 crore higher depreciation. Management said Q2 was hit by US tariffs and that a manpower shortage cost about INR 80 crore of sales in the quarter, now reportedly resolved after 20 May. Management guides FY27 PAT growth of 15-20%, EBITDA per wheel near INR 300 and EBITDA of about INR 650 crore, with upside bias.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 EBITDA incl. other income

financial_highlights.value: INR 262 (flat YoY); about INR 272 cited elsewhere in call
financial_highlights.change: flat; ex export and Chennai effects about INR 274
slightly lower YoY, due to about INR 28 crore higher depreciation

segments.name: Alloy wheels
segments.commentary: Value grew about 30% in FY26 and now contribute about 36% of total revenue; volume growth is single-digit while value growth is double-digit due to aluminium price pass-through. Aluminium knuckles capacity added to about 0.5 million, with business still early-stage.

segments.name: Tractor wheels
segments.commentary: Grew about 19% per management; described as a high-value, steady-volume segment. Tractor share of steel wheel end-user mix is about 13%.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle (truck) wheels
segments.commentary: Grew about 10% in FY26, held back by a sharp Q2 slump; CV is about 28% of the mix per management.

segments.name: Passenger car and MUV
segments.commentary: About 54% of the mix including alloy and steel wheels, per management. Steel wheel pricing for OEM contracts was reset upward after a large OEM accepted increases.

segments.name: EV two/three-wheeler wheels
segments.commentary: Management claims about 80% share of EV scooter wheels and about 30% share of ICE two-wheeler wheels; May 2026 was the highest EV segment sales month, with FY27 EV growth guided at 25% or more, possibly near 40%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT growth of about 15-20%, premised on running plants at near 100% utilisation.
FY27 EBITDA per wheel close to INR 300 (vs INR 262-272 in FY26), with an upward bias, and EBITDA of about INR 650 crore (plus or minus), possibly higher.
FY27 turnover expected near INR 6,500 crore vs INR 5,143 crore cited for this year; FY28 EBITDA range INR 700-750 crore, with the Bhuj projects adding INR 700-800 crore of revenue as they ramp.
Exports expected at about INR 600 crore in FY27, up from about INR 454 crore in FY26.
Utilisation target of 95% across assets in the current year, versus 76-78% steel plant utilisation last year.
Debt to rise by about INR 200 crore in FY27 for modelling purposes, to be reviewed at end-September; FY27 capex about INR 500 crore plus about INR 50 crore brownfield.
capex_capacity: Bhuj (AMW facility) aluminium wheel project of about 1.2 million wheels, bringing aluminium wheel capacity to about 6.2 million; trial runs expected from October, running to about January; commissioning targeted by year-end.

Bhuj aluminium knuckles project of about 1.1 million, in two phases (about 600k then 500k); phase one at about 1.2 million by year-end and a further 0.5 million next year. Total Bhuj capex about INR 500 crore.

Management said Bhuj revenue cannot be quantified yet because it depends on OEM approvals; FY28 utilisation guided at about 70% or higher, and management said knuckles could reach near 100% next year.
Steel wheel brownfield: tractor capacity to rise by about 15-20%, two paint shops added, and rim lines planned at Chandigarh for October-December; car line expansion still under discussion.
Management said the Bhuj aluminium project is about four to five months later than originally planned.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand strong after October GST cuts; management says the company has gained market share and that the company is the top two in India.
Management says Q4 monthly run rate is close to INR 500 crore; June 2026 is expected to be the highest sales month.
Manpower shortage cost about INR 80 crore of sales in the quarter; management says there was zero shortage after 20 May.

Aluminium prices reportedly up about 20% with another 10% expected; OEMs may shift some car wheels to steel. Management says raw material costs are passed through, now generally in the same month rather than with a three-month lag.
Steel wheel OEM pricing was reset upward after a large OEM accepted increases; the price gap between aluminium (about INR 5,000 per wheel) and steel car wheels (about INR 1,200) was cited.
Exports fell about 19% in FY26 due to US tariffs; management says tariffs are now similar across nations and a US trade deal and anti-dumping cases against Southeast Asian competitors are supportive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 EBITDA per wheel and how does it compare to expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 EBITDA per wheel was INR 282, above expectations, and that the FY27 target of near INR 300 is based on that exit rate.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Bhuj facilities ramp and what revenue do they add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the projects add about INR 700-800 crore of top-line at full utilisation, with approvals pending; FY28 utilisation is guided at about 70% or higher.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt evolve and what are the FY27 turnover and EBITDA numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management asked modellers to assume about INR 200 crore higher debt in FY27, with FY27 turnover near INR 6,500 crore and EBITDA of INR 650-750 crore across FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV two- and three-wheeler opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company holds about 80% of EV scooter wheels and about 30% of ICE two-wheeler wheels, with EV growth guided at 25% or more in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much aluminium cost increase has been passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material costs are passed through in the same month, and that the company needs more working capital while OEMs accept the increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the end-user mix and realisation gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a mix of car and MUV at 54%, CV at 28%, tractor at 13%, OTR at 1%, two/three-wheeler at 2% and knuckles at 1%; the realisation gap between steel and aluminium wheels is about INR 3,000-4,000.

risks_watch: Labour availability: management says manpower was the largest constraint and cost about INR 80 crore of sales in Q4; the 20 May stabilisation claim needs confirmation in Q1 FY27.
Bhuj approvals from OEMs: revenue timing is uncertain and the project is already about four to five months behind.
Utilisation target of 95% across assets is a stretch versus 76-78% last year; the FY27 EBITDA guidance is premised on it.
Export recovery to about INR 600 crore depends on the US trade deal and on ramp-up of European, Latin American and Asian nominations.
Energy, steel, paint and aluminium cost inflation, with working capital needs rising; management says pass-through is in place but timing and scale are unverified.
Chennai facility under-utilisation raised costs in FY26; the company has not quantified the ongoing effect.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on demand, margins and utilisation, with the CEO repeatedly framing FY27 as the strongest year in company history. Management was less precise on Bhuj revenue timing, debt, and export numbers, and corrected some figures on the call (for example, last year's exports).
key_quotes: Finally, I'm very pleased to share with you that we have delivered our highest-ever revenue, registering a growth of 17% YoY.
Our raw material costs are a pass through. Whether it rains or shines, the situation remains the same for us.
I think the margin profile from INR 300 should be higher, maybe another 10% on a conservative estimate in 2027, 2028.
